_about: T-101 M6 exit: the PLAN.md §1 M6 exit items and the PRD §8 scenarios of the M6 requirements mapped to the exact test cases that prove each (JUnit classname = file, name = 'describe > test'). Checked by check-scenarios.py against a JUnit report of `pnpm test -- m6`: every required scenario and exit item mapped; every title a PRD §8 scenario; every mapped name in its file; every mapped case present once and passed; no failure anywhere. 'proves' states what the cases assert; 'open' what M6 does not prove and what completes it.

tests: T-089 scenario PR-27 (Embedded Signup → numbers → the cap → verification) > connects, seals the token, registers two numbers, refuses the third until verified
scenarios.proves: an unverified business holds at two numbers; the third asks for Meta business verification; verified, it goes through (T-089)
scenarios.open: live Meta Embedded Signup (mock Graph port only until the Tech Provider app is approved; DEC-082)

tests: T-090 scenario PR-28 (the 24 h window) > 25 h after the last patient message: free-form refused, only approved templates; marketing needs consent
scenarios.proves: 25 h after the last patient message free-form is refused and only approved templates send; marketing templates need consent (T-090)

tests: T-092 scenario PR-29 (converted requires payment) > new → contacted → booked → arrived; converted refused until a payment exists, then converts
scenarios.proves: a lead that arrived but paid nothing cannot be marked converted; once paid it converts (T-092)

tests: T-093 Scenario PR-30 (control due) > a free control two days away creates one task for the guiding BC; three days away none; a closed task is not re-created
scenarios.proves: a free control two days away creates one task for the guiding BC (T-093)

tests: T-094 Scenario PR-31 (daily budget) > the budget reached: new recipients stay queued for the next window, the backlog shows them; a known recipient still sends
scenarios.proves: the daily budget reached: more due messages stay queued for the next window and the backlog shows them (T-094)

tests: T-091 scenario PR-43 inbox flag > CS flags the message clinical: a task for the Kemang clinicians, the doctor reads it, CS sees only its status
scenarios.proves: the inbox flag part: CS flags a WhatsApp message clinical → a task for the clinicians on duty; CS sees only its status (T-091; the visit-note flag was M2)

tests: T-095 Scenario PR-69 (reminder reply) > a booking tomorrow: the H-1 reminder is sent at 10:00 with neutral params; the patient taps Konfirmasi → the appointment is confirmed
scenarios.proves: a booking tomorrow, the reminder sent, the patient replies Konfirmasi → the appointment shows confirmed (T-095)

tests: T-096 Scenario PR-70 (aftercare) > a closed visit with aftercare → a neutral notice without marketing consent; the link opens the texts only after the WhatsApp OTP
scenarios.proves: the visit closes → a neutral care message with a protected link is sent without marketing consent and without the treatment name (T-096)

tests: T-098 Scenario PR-78 (low score) > a patient scores 2 of 5 → a manager task is created and no review request is sent
scenarios.proves: a score of 2 creates a manager task and no review request is sent (T-098)
scenarios.open: the survey page, the WhatsApp survey reply and the branch review link (DEC-110 (5); a hygiene task proposed)

tests: T-099 Scenario PR-81 > a patient waits for a service; a matching slot is cancelled → the entry is offered that slot and the branch's FO / CS / manager are prompted
scenarios.proves: a matching cancelled slot prompts the branch's staff to offer it (T-099)
scenarios.open: the Daftar Tunggu page and hold expiry (DEC-111 (5))

tests: T-097 Scenario PR-94 (frequency cap) > two automated messages today → a third scenario is queued for the next day, shown as capped
scenarios.proves: a patient with two automated messages today: a third scenario is queued for the next day (T-097)

tests: T-100 Scenario PR-94: campaign sending gated > a scheduled campaign to a consented segment; Q-15 evidence not approved → refused with the copy, nothing queued, segment editable
scenarios.proves: a scheduled campaign to a consented segment is refused with the copy while the Q-15 evidence is not approved; the segment stays editable (T-100)
scenarios.open: campaign sending itself until counsel clears Q-15 (PR-97 evidence; owner)

items.item: M6 exit: webhook replay fixtures (duplicate, late, out of order, bad signature)
tests: M6 exit: webhook replay fixtures on the test number > duplicate, out of order, late and bad signature deliveries
items.proves: on the test number: the same inbound twice → one message; a bad signature → 401 and no event id claimed, the genuine delivery then processes; a status before its message → held and applied; a late inbound never moves the window back

items.item: M6 exit: webhook replay fixtures (per-task intake)
tests: T-090 webhook intake (TD-22) and the replay fixtures > an inbound message creates one conversation at the number's branch, sealed; a duplicate delivery adds nothing
T-090 webhook intake (TD-22) and the replay fixtures > a bad signature is refused (401) and claims no event id; the real delivery then processes
T-090 webhook intake (TD-22) and the replay fixtures > statuses advance only; one that arrives before its message is held and applied; a late inbound never moves the window back
items.proves: the same four replay cases at the intake's own test (T-090)

items.item: M6 exit: PR-94 per-patient cap under concurrency
tests: M6 exit: the test number end to end (recorded fixtures, mock ports) > 12 the per-patient cap under concurrency (PR-94): automation-style enqueue and campaign_send overlap on one patient with one slot left
items.proves: isolated: approved synthetic Q-15 evidence, consent, a wide budget, one slot left on D; an automation-style writer holding staff_access + the cap lock and campaign_send overlap (pg_blocking_pids); the automation message takes D, the campaign message D+1; dispatch on D sends 2 (the cap; care counts, never deferred), on D+1 the campaign

T-097 Scenario PR-94 (frequency cap) > two automation scans at once (no lock held by the test) for one patient with one slot left: the cap holds
